chips.text: Ensures representation for Deaf and Hard of Hearing community on committee.

chips.text: Downtown Business Improvement District gains committee representation.

description: Councillor MacDonald appointed as City of Saskatoon representative to CUTA.
Sets electric vehicle charging fee at $5.35 per hour.

chips.text: Staff analysis showed demand for EV charging would drop over 50% at $5.35/hour.
Saskatoon taxpayers will subsidize the stations by $4,000-$8,000 annually.
The percentage of city vehicles that are electric was not known.
Public feedback indicated interest in using the charging stations.
Councillor MacDonald preferred $3/hour to incentivize EV adoption and align with other cities.
High fees could reduce demand, countering climate change mitigation goals.
Administration will report back in one year to reassess the charging station decision.

description: City's 2024 financial statements show $298.4 million surplus.

chips.text: Councillor Pearce questioned how 2022-2023 capital expenditures were missed and new safeguards.
Land developers contribute to city's surplus and fund new infrastructure.
Staff committed to monthly reviews and new processes for recording reserve entries.
